II. Open Source Operating Systems — Definition and Examples
Open source OS: operating system whose source code is freely available to study, modify and
redistribute under an open license (GPL, BSD, Apache).
Examples: LINUX (Ubuntu, Fedora, Debian), FreeBSD, OpenBSD, Android (AOSP), ReactOS, MINIX.
Advantages: transparency, community support, no licence cost, customizability, security auditing.
